title: Ark Invest Buys $96 Million of SpaceX, Adds Nvidia and AMD, Trims Broadcom
excerpt: Cathie Wood's funds recorded $346.2 million in purchases against $305.8 million in sales last week, buying the chip sell-off and funding it mainly with a $122.2 million Broadcom sale.
body:
• Cathie Wood's Ark Invest bought $96.0 million of SpaceX stock across ARKK, ARKQ and ARKW last week, its largest purchase, while selling $122.2 million of Broadcom, its largest sale, according to Ark's disclosures as reported by Seeking Alpha.
  • Ark also added $45.9 million of Nvidia and $20.0 million of AMD, buying into a sharp semiconductor sell-off in which Nvidia fell about 9% and AMD about 17% on November 5.
  • Across its actively managed ETFs, Ark recorded $346.2 million in gross purchases and $305.8 million in gross sales for the week.
  • SpaceX was already ARKK's largest holding at $410.80 million, or 7.28% of the fund, as of November 5.

Cathie Wood used last week's tech sell-off to buy. Ark Invest's largest purchase across its actively managed ETFs was $96.0 million of Space Exploration Technologies (SpaceX, traded as SPCX) across the ARKK, ARKQ and ARKW funds, and its largest sale was $122.2 million of Broadcom, according to Ark's trading disclosures reported by Seeking Alpha. In total the firm recorded $346.2 million in gross purchases and $305.8 million in gross sales for the week.

Buying the chip dip

In semiconductors, Ark bought $45.9 million of Nvidia and $20.0 million of Advanced Micro Devices, plus $17.2 million of Cerebras Systems. The timing was deliberate dip-buying: on November 5, as investors reacted to the midterm results and worried about limits on AI data-centre expansion, Nvidia fell 9.26% and AMD fell 17.26% in a single session. Ark's daily disclosures for that day show purchases of 252,592 Nvidia shares, and TipRanks reported the funds also bought 393,774 SpaceX shares worth about $48.7 million and 48,984 AMD shares on November 5 alone.

What Ark sold to pay for it

Broadcom led the week's sales at $122.2 million; TipRanks put the November 5 portion at 410,559 shares worth about $119.7 million, on a day Broadcom fell 10.43%. Ark also sold 412,666 CoreWeave shares worth about $20 million that day, and reduced positions including Teradyne during the week, Seeking Alpha reported. Other purchases included Rocket Lab — 276,925 shares worth about $12.74 million on November 5, per TipRanks — and Alphabet.

SpaceX is already the flagship's anchor

The week's buying deepens a position Ark already leaned on. As of November 5, SpaceX was the Ark Innovation ETF's largest holding at $410.80 million, or 7.28% of the fund, with Nvidia second among the names listed at $209.02 million, or 3.70%. The pattern is consistent with Wood's stated approach of treating broad sell-offs as entry points into her highest-conviction names — here, space and AI chips funded by trimming a chip name, Broadcom, that she was less willing to add to at the lows.

Ark publishes its trades daily, so the next disclosures will show whether the rebalancing persisted or was a one-week reaction to the sell-off. The figures above are the firm's reported trades for last week, not a recommendation: ARKK's five-year annualised return to November 5 was negative even as it made these purchases, a reminder that conviction and performance are different things.
